title: The Governance Point independently re-verifies the Spell against the Executive Sheet in both directions after deployment
content:
After handover, A.1.10.2.4.11.1.1 requires the Governance Point to run six checks: that all Executive Sheet items "are accurately reflected in the Spell code"; that all values match; that "no items are present in the Spell code that are not included in the Executive Sheet, **with limited exceptions such as approvals or other predefined standard actions**"; that reviews were submitted by the designated reviewers; that "the deployed code matches the corresponding code in the GitHub repository"; and that "reviewers have approved the deployed code at the specified handover address."

This is a fourth independent pass over the same correspondence — after the Crafter built it, the Reviewers approved it twice, and the Content Liaisons confirmed the values — and it is performed by the governance role rather than an engineering one. It is also anchored to the Executive Sheet, complementing the Reviewers' Document-anchored check, so both reference artifacts get tested against the code by different parties.

The negative check is again the security-relevant one, and its exception deserves attention. "Limited exceptions such as approvals or other predefined standard actions" is the single place in this chain where code may legitimately exist without a corresponding sheet entry. Any smuggled action would have to look like a routine approval to survive here, which is a narrow but real gap — and it is unclear who maintains the list of what counts as "predefined standard."

The last two checks are about the chain rather than the content: deployed bytecode versus repository source, and approvals attached to the specific handover address. Together they prevent a correct review of correct code from being redirected onto a different deployed contract.
description: A.1.10.2.4.11.1.1 adds a non-Spell-Team check that nothing is missing and nothing extra is present, with a carve-out for approvals and other predefined standard actions.
